PHASE 09 / BOOK 01

Prisma Mental Model & Architecture
Understand every Prisma layer before installing it

NestJS

PrismaService

Prisma Client

PrismaPg driver adapter

Supabase PostgreSQL

Figure - The database access stack introduced in Phase 09

Course rule: Prisma CLI, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg are locked to 7.9.1. Newer Prisma releases are not
substituted halfway through the course.

1. Why Add an ORM Now?
We deliberately waited. If Prisma had appeared before SQL, keys, constraints, joins and transactions, database
behavior would look like framework magic. Phase 07 and 08 removed that mystery. Prisma can now be understood as
a typed programming interface over relational database work.

NestJS service asks for data

Prisma Client builds a typed query

PrismaPg sends PostgreSQL protocol
traffic

PostgreSQL executes the query

Plain JavaScript data returns

Figure 1 - Runtime query lifecycle

2. Prisma Is Several Things, Not One Thing
Piece                       Responsibility                                           Not responsible for

prisma CLI                  init, validate, generate, migrate, studio                Serving HTTP requests

schema.prisma               Data models + generator + DB provider                    Storing credentials in Prisma 7

prisma.config.ts            CLI configuration and datasource URL                     Runtime NestJS DI

Prisma Client               Generated type-safe query API                            Hosting PostgreSQL

PrismaPg                    Driver adapter using pg                                  Business rules

PrismaService               NestJS provider wrapping one client instance             HTTP route design

PostgreSQL                  Actual persistent relational database                    TypeScript types

3. Runtime vs Tooling Paths

Runtime path                                                             Tooling path
NestJS                                                                   pnpm exec prisma
PrismaService                                                            prisma.config.ts
Prisma Client                                                            DIRECT_URL
PrismaPg                                                                 Migrate / Studio / introspection
DATABASE_URL                                                             PostgreSQL
PostgreSQL

Figure 2 - Two connection purposes in the same project

This distinction matters with Supabase. The long-running application can use a pooled runtime connection while
migration tooling uses a session-capable or direct connection. The same database may be targeted, but the
connection behavior and privilege requirements differ.

4. The NestJS Boundary
Controllers should still handle HTTP. Services still own business rules. PrismaService is infrastructure: it gives
application services a reusable database client. A controller should not become a place where authentication,
ownership, query construction and response formatting are all mixed together.

TodosController

TodosService

PrismaService

Prisma Client

PostgreSQL

Figure 3 - Database access stays below application logic

5. What Prisma Does Not Replace
• Database constraints: PostgreSQL remains the final integrity boundary.

• Authorization: Prisma will execute a query you ask for; it does not decide whether a user should be allowed to make it.

• Business logic: status transitions, approvals, payroll rules and domain policies still belong in application services.

• SQL understanding: indexes, transactions, joins and query shape still matter.

• Migrations review: generated SQL must still be inspected, especially for destructive changes.

Checkpoint
You are ready for installation when you can describe Prisma as a typed database access layer rather than as "the
database".

PHASE 09 / BOOK 02

Install & Lock Prisma 7.9.1
Exact dependencies, local CLI and reproducible tooling

NestJS

PrismaService

Prisma Client

PrismaPg driver adapter

Supabase PostgreSQL

Figure - The database access stack introduced in Phase 09

Course rule: Prisma CLI, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg are locked to 7.9.1. Newer Prisma releases are not
substituted halfway through the course.

1. Work From the API Package
All Prisma database tooling stays inside apps/api for now. We do not create packages/database merely because the
repository has a packages folder. The backend is currently the only owner of database access.
PowerShell - verify location

Get-Location
# Expected path ends with: taskflow\apps\api

2. Install Exact Versions
PowerShell - install the locked Prisma stack

# From: taskflow\apps\api
pnpm add -D prisma@7.9.1 @types/pg
pnpm add @prisma/client@7.9.1 @prisma/adapter-pg@7.9.1 pg dotenv @nestjs/config

The CLI is a development dependency. The generated client runtime, adapter and pg driver are runtime dependencies
because the NestJS API uses them while running.

Package responsibilities
Package                             Type              Why it exists

prisma@7.9.1                        dev               CLI: init, validate, generate, migrate, studio

@prisma/client@7.9.1                runtime           Runtime package used by generated Prisma Client

@prisma/adapter-pg@7.9.1            runtime           Prisma 7 PostgreSQL driver adapter

pg                                  runtime           Underlying PostgreSQL driver

dotenv                              runtime/tooling   Loads .env for Prisma config/scripts

@nestjs/config                      runtime           Loads trusted backend configuration into Nest DI

@types/pg                           dev               TypeScript declarations for pg when needed

3. Verify the Local CLI
PowerShell - use the project-local CLI

# From: taskflow\apps\api
pnpm exec prisma version

Do not rely on a globally installed prisma executable. pnpm exec resolves the version declared by this project, which is
exactly the reproducibility we want in a long course.

EXPECTED
The Prisma CLI line and @prisma/client line should report 7.9.1. Stop if one package reports a different version.

4. pnpm Build Approval
If pnpm reports ignored dependency build scripts, treat that as a supply-chain security decision rather than a broken
install.
PowerShell - only if pnpm tells you builds were ignored

pnpm approve-builds

Approve only packages that are actually required by this project. Do not globally disable script protection.

5. Why Exact Versions Matter
• Generated Client code is tied to the Prisma generation toolchain.

• Breaking CLI/config behavior can change across major releases.

• A course that silently upgrades becomes impossible to debug because two learners can follow the same page and get
different generated output.

• Locking versions turns documentation into a reproducible engineering artifact.

Checkpoint
Verify all three course-critical packages

pnpm exec prisma version
pnpm list prisma @prisma/client @prisma/adapter-pg

lessons.body:
PHASE 09 / BOOK 03

prisma init & File Anatomy
Understand the files before editing them

NestJS

PrismaService

Prisma Client

PrismaPg driver adapter

Supabase PostgreSQL

Figure - The database access stack introduced in Phase 09

Course rule: Prisma CLI, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg are locked to 7.9.1. Newer Prisma releases are not
substituted halfway through the course.

1. Initialize Prisma
Initialization creates the Prisma workspace inside apps/api. It does not create your production architecture, and it does
not replace the database you already created in Supabase.
PowerShell - initialize Prisma inside apps/api

# From: taskflow\apps\api
pnpm exec prisma init

2. What prisma init Creates
apps/api/.env

apps/api/prisma.config.ts

apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma

Figure 1 - The three pieces to inspect after initialization

.env
Stores local environment values. It must never be committed with real secrets.

prisma.config.ts
Configures Prisma CLI behavior in Prisma 7, including the schema path, migration directory and the connection URL
used by CLI commands.

prisma/schema.prisma
Defines the database provider, generated client and data models. In Prisma 7, the datasource URL no longer belongs
here for this course.

3. Project Structure After Initialization
Relevant paths only

apps/api/
|-- .env
|-- prisma.config.ts
|-- prisma/
|   `-- schema.prisma
|-- src/
|-- package.json
`-- ...

4. Do Not Re-run init as a Fix
Once these files exist, errors should be diagnosed in place. Re-running initialization can overwrite assumptions or
encourage deleting the evidence you need to debug.

5. Update the Example Environment File
apps/api/.env.example

# Runtime application connection (Phase 08 recommends a session-capable pooled URL for local NestJS).
DATABASE_URL=

# Prisma CLI / migration connection. Prefer a direct URL when reachable.
DIRECT_URL=

# Optional only if migrate dev cannot create an automatic shadow database.
# NEVER point this at the same database as DIRECT_URL.
SHADOW_DATABASE_URL=

SECRET RULE
Real DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL and SHADOW_DATABASE_URL values belong only in .env or a secure
deployment secret store. They never belong in screenshots, documentation, Git commits or NEXT_PUBLIC_*
variables.

Checkpoint
• prisma.config.ts exists.

• prisma/schema.prisma exists.

• .env exists locally and is ignored.

• .env.example documents variable names but contains no credentials.

lessons.body:
PHASE 09 / BOOK 04

Schema, Generator & First Model
Prisma Schema Language without hiding the relational model

NestJS

PrismaService

Prisma Client

PrismaPg driver adapter

Supabase PostgreSQL

Figure - The database access stack introduced in Phase 09

Course rule: Prisma CLI, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg are locked to 7.9.1. Newer Prisma releases are not
substituted halfway through the course.

1. The Prisma Schema Has Three Responsibilities
At this point schema.prisma describes: the client generator, the database provider and the first minimal application
model. Credentials stay outside this file.
apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma

generator client {
provider     = "prisma-client"
output       = "../src/generated/prisma"
moduleFormat = "cjs"
}

datasource db {
provider = "postgresql"
}

model Todo {
id         String  @id @default(cuid())
title      String
completed Boolean @default(false)
createdAt DateTime @default(now())
updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

2. Generator Block
provider = "prisma-client" selects Prisma 7's generated TypeScript client. output is required in Prisma 7 and places
generated code under src/generated/prisma so Nest's TypeScript build can see it.

NESTJS MODULE FORMAT
This course keeps the existing NestJS CommonJS build. moduleFormat = "cjs" aligns the generated Prisma
Client with that build instead of converting the entire backend to ESM midway through the course.

3. Datasource Block
The datasource says only that PostgreSQL is the database provider. The connection URL is handled by
prisma.config.ts in Prisma 7.

4. First Minimal Todo Model
This model exists only to teach the migration and client-generation workflow. Phase 10 will revisit the relational design
before the production CRUD phase.

Field                    Meaning                                           Database concept

id                       Application identifier generated as a cuid        Primary key

title                    Required task title                               NOT NULL text

completed                Defaults false                                    Boolean + default

createdAt                Creation timestamp                                Default now()

updatedAt                Updated by Prisma on writes                       Application-managed timestamp

5. Validate Before Migrating
From: taskflow\apps\api

pnpm exec prisma validate

Validation checks Prisma configuration/schema correctness. It is not a substitute for reviewing migration SQL and it
does not prove that every runtime query works.

Checkpoint
Do not continue until prisma validate succeeds and you can explain why moduleFormat, output and datasource
provider are separate decisions.

lessons.body:
PHASE 09 / BOOK 05

Prisma Config, Supabase URLs &
Shadow Database
Separate runtime traffic from migration tooling

NestJS

PrismaService

Prisma Client

PrismaPg driver adapter

Supabase PostgreSQL

Figure - The database access stack introduced in Phase 09

Course rule: Prisma CLI, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg are locked to 7.9.1. Newer Prisma releases are not
substituted halfway through the course.

1. Prisma CLI and NestJS Runtime Have Different
Connection Jobs

NestJS runtime                                                         Prisma CLI
Uses DATABASE_URL                                                      Uses DIRECT_URL
Long-running application traffic                                       Migrations / introspection / Studio
PrismaPg / pg pool                                                     Needs session semantics
Session-capable pooled URL works                                       migrate dev also needs shadow DB
well locally

Figure 1 - Separate the runtime and tooling connection roles

2. Configure prisma.config.ts
apps/api/prisma.config.ts

import "dotenv/config";
import { defineConfig, env } from "prisma/config";

export default defineConfig({
schema: "prisma/schema.prisma",
migrations: {
path: "prisma/migrations",
},
datasource: {
// CLI / migrations: direct or session-capable connection.
url: env("DIRECT_URL"),
},
});

The CLI now reads DIRECT_URL. For Supabase, prefer the direct database URL when your network can reach it. A
session pooler connection on port 5432 is an alternative when direct IPv6 connectivity is unavailable. Do not use
transaction pooling for migration tooling.

3. Environment Variables
apps/api/.env.example

# Runtime application connection (Phase 08 recommends a session-capable pooled URL for local NestJS).
DATABASE_URL=

# Prisma CLI / migration connection. Prefer a direct URL when reachable.
DIRECT_URL=

# Optional only if migrate dev cannot create an automatic shadow database.
# NEVER point this at the same database as DIRECT_URL.
SHADOW_DATABASE_URL=

4. Why migrate dev Needs a Shadow Database
Prisma Migrate replays migration history in a temporary shadow database to detect drift and evaluate the next
migration. That means migrate dev needs either permission to create/drop a shadow database automatically or a
separately configured shadow database.

Migration history

Shadow database replay

Detect drift / evaluate changes

Generate SQL migration

Apply to development database

Figure 2 - migrate dev uses a shadow database before changing your dev schema

DANGER
SHADOW_DATABASE_URL must never point to the same database as DIRECT_URL. A shadow database is
reset during migrate dev and can destroy data if misconfigured.

5. Supabase Privileges
Supabase's current Prisma guidance recommends a dedicated Prisma database user with the privileges required for
migrations, including CREATEDB when automatic shadow-database creation is used. Keep this as a
development/migration concern; application runtime access should still follow least privilege as the course matures.

6. If Automatic Shadow Creation Fails
Do not immediately switch to db push and ignore migration history. First diagnose whether the database user has
CREATEDB. If cloud restrictions prevent automatic shadow creation, create a dedicated shadow database and set
SHADOW_DATABASE_URL in prisma.config.ts.
Optional prisma.config.ts change

datasource: {
url: env("DIRECT_URL"),
shadowDatabaseUrl: env("SHADOW_DATABASE_URL"),
},

Checkpoint
• DATABASE_URL is reserved for runtime PrismaPg.

• DIRECT_URL is used by Prisma CLI/migrations.

• Transaction pooler 6543 is not used for migration tooling.

• Shadow DB configuration is understood before migrate dev is run.

Migration Lifecycle & First Migration
Create schema history you can inspect, commit and deploy

Course rule: Prisma CLI, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg are locked to 7.9.1. Newer Prisma releases are not
substituted halfway through the course.

1. Migration Is Schema History, Not a Magic Sync Button
The Prisma schema is the desired model. A migration is an ordered SQL change that moves a database from one
known state to another. Keeping that history in Git is what makes team and deployment workflows reproducible.

Edit schema.prisma

Validate

migrate dev creates SQL

Review migration.sql

Apply to development DB

Run prisma generate

Commit schema + migration

Figure 1 - Safe development migration workflow

2. Create the First Migration
From: taskflow\apps\api

pnpm exec prisma migrate dev --name init_todo

If Prisma asks to reset a database containing data you care about, stop. Do not confirm reflexively. A reset is
destructive and should be understood before proceeding.

3. Inspect the Generated SQL
Generated migration directory

prisma/
`-- migrations/
`-- <timestamp>_init_todo/
`-- migration.sql

Open migration.sql. Compare it with the SQL concepts learned in Phase 07: CREATE TABLE, primary key, required
columns and defaults. Prisma migrations are not opaque binary files; they are reviewable SQL.

4. The _prisma_migrations Table
Prisma records applied migration metadata in the database so tooling can compare migration history with the actual
development database.

5. Explicit Client Generation
Run after migration/schema changes

pnpm exec prisma generate

PRISMA 7 COURSE RULE
Run prisma generate explicitly. This avoids relying on version-specific assumptions about migrate dev side
effects and makes the build step obvious to the learner.

6. Migration Status
From: taskflow\apps\api

pnpm exec prisma migrate status

7. Development vs Production
Environment                           Command                    Purpose

Development                           prisma migrate dev         Create + apply migrations, detect drift, uses shadow DB

Production / staging                  prisma migrate deploy      Apply already-committed pending migrations; do not generate new schema de

Any stage                             prisma migrate status      Inspect migration state

8. Never Edit an Applied Shared Migration Casually
Once a migration has been applied and shared with teammates or environments, rewriting it changes history. Fix
forward with a new migration unless you are deliberately resetting an isolated development database.

Checkpoint
• The migration directory exists.

• migration.sql was manually inspected.

• The migration applied only to the intended development database.

• prisma migrate status reports a clean state.

• The generated client was refreshed.

1. The CLI Commands You Should Actually Remember
Command                                                       When to use it

pnpm exec prisma version                                      Confirm exact local toolchain

pnpm exec prisma validate                                     Check config/schema syntax

pnpm exec prisma generate                                     Regenerate typed client

pnpm exec prisma migrate dev --name ...                       Create/apply development migration

pnpm exec prisma migrate status                               Inspect migration state

pnpm exec prisma migrate deploy                               Apply committed migrations in production/staging

pnpm exec prisma studio                                       Inspect/edit data interactively in development

2. A Normal Schema Change Loop
Edit                   Validate                  Migrate                    Review                 Generate                  Build

Change schema.prisma     Catch schema/config       Generate/apply SQL        Read migration.sql       Refresh client types   Nest production build
mistakes

Figure 1 - Repeat this loop as the model evolves

Example development sequence

pnpm exec prisma validate
pnpm exec prisma migrate dev --name add_due_date
pnpm exec prisma generate
pnpm run build

3. Prisma Studio
Studio is a developer inspection tool, not an application admin panel. It is useful for confirming that tables and rows
look as expected while learning, but production business operations still belong behind application authorization and
audit rules.
From: taskflow\apps\api

pnpm exec prisma studio

4. db push Has a Different Job
db push synchronizes a schema without creating migration history. It can be useful for disposable prototypes, but
TaskFlow is a course about production-style development, so migrations remain the default once schema history
matters.

DO NOT NORMALIZE DESTRUCTIVE FLAGS
Avoid treating --accept-data-loss or reset confirmations as routine. Destructive operations require understanding
the target environment and the data being discarded.

5. Build Pipeline Implication
Because Prisma 7 generates client code to a project directory, deployments must ensure generate runs before the
TypeScript build if generated output is not committed. A later CI/CD phase will make that automated and repeatable.

6. Production Rule
Production should receive migration files that were created and reviewed during development. Production is not where
you improvise a new migration by running migrate dev.

Checkpoint
You should be able to decide which Prisma command to use without searching for a random tutorial each time.

Debugging Prisma & Common Failures

NestJS

PrismaService

Prisma Client

Figure - The database access stack introduced in Phase 09

Course rule: Prisma CLI, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg are locked to 7.9.1. Newer Prisma releases are not
substituted halfway through the course.

1. Debug Prisma by Layer
Working directory / local package

Prisma config

Schema + generator

Generated client

Driver adapter

Connection URL / network

PostgreSQL privileges / schema

Figure 1 - Start at the failing layer instead of rewriting the project

2. Wrong Version or Global CLI
Use the project-local CLI

pnpm exec prisma version

If versions differ from 7.9.1, inspect package.json and the lockfile. Do not "fix" the docs to match a newer package
accidentally installed.

3. Generated Client Module Error
Symptoms may mention exports, require, ESM or module scope. In this NestJS CommonJS course, confirm the
generator contains moduleFormat = "cjs" and regenerate the client.
Regenerate after generator changes

pnpm exec prisma generate

4. PrismaClient Requires an Adapter
Prisma 7 direct database connections require a driver adapter. If the code constructs PrismaClient without PrismaPg,
fix the construction path instead of downgrading packages.

5. DATABASE_URL vs DIRECT_URL Confusion
Symptom                                                 Likely layer

Nest API cannot query but CLI works                     DATABASE_URL / runtime adapter

migrate/status fails but API query works                DIRECT_URL / Prisma CLI path

Browser fetch fails before API query                    HTTP/CORS, not Prisma

P1001 / connection timeout                              Network/host/port/SSL

Shadow database permission error                        CREATEDB or SHADOW_DATABASE_URL

6. Shadow Database Failure
If migrate dev reports permission denied to create database, verify the migration user privileges. If automatic creation
is not allowed, configure a dedicated shadow database. Never reuse the development database as the shadow target.

7. Pooled Connection Mistakes
Transaction pooling is optimized for different workloads and does not preserve all session behavior migration tools
expect. Use a direct or session-capable connection for Prisma CLI migration workflows.

8. Schema Changed but TypeScript Did Not
The generated client is stale. Run prisma generate and rebuild. Schema changes do not magically rewrite TypeScript
imports already produced on disk.

9. "Relation Does Not Exist"
Check migration status and target database/schema. A perfectly typed generated client can still point at a database
where the migration was never applied.

10. Common Anti-Patterns
• Creating new PrismaClient instances in controller methods.

• Putting DATABASE_URL into NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables.

• Using migrate dev in production.

• Ignoring migration SQL without review.

• Using db push to avoid learning migrations in a production-style project.

• Deleting the migrations directory whenever drift appears.

• Mixing Prisma 8 docs into this locked 7.9.1 course.

• Treating Prisma validation as authorization or business validation.

Checkpoint
When a Prisma failure appears, identify whether it is tooling, generated code, adapter/runtime, network, privilege or
database state before changing anything.

Architecture trace
schema.prisma -> migration files -> database schema -> generated Prisma Client -> PrismaService -> feature service

Read this flow left to right, then right to left. For each arrow, say what data crosses the boundary, which side trusts the other, and what evidence would prove that this boundary works. This habit prevents framework APIs from becoming disconnected memorization.

Debugging Workshop — Phase 09: Prisma 7.9.1 Architecture, Configuration & Migrations

Goal
Learn to diagnose this phase's failures systematically instead of reinstalling packages, changing random configuration, or copying a fix without understanding it.

The debugging loop
1. Reproduce the failure with the smallest reliable action.
2. Capture the exact symptom: command, status code, stack trace, network request, database state, or UI state.
3. Locate the earliest boundary where actual behavior diverges from expected behavior.
4. Form one hypothesis.
5. Change one variable.
6. Re-run the same reproduction.
7. Keep the fix only if the evidence supports the hypothesis.

Boundary walk
schema.prisma -> migration files -> database schema -> generated Prisma Client -> PrismaService -> feature service

Start at the visible symptom and walk backward. Do not debug the database when the browser never sent the request. Do not debug React state when the API is returning a deterministic 403. The boundary walk tells you which evidence to collect next.

Failure drill 1 — CLI/client version mismatch
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 2 — Editing generated client code
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Do not hide the evidence
Avoid immediately clearing caches, deleting lockfiles, resetting the database, disabling security checks, or reinstalling everything. Those actions may erase the evidence that teaches you what was wrong. Use them only after you can explain why they are relevant.

Debugging exit ticket
Pick one failure from this workshop and write a short incident note: symptom, scope, root cause, fix, verification, and prevention. This is the same communication pattern used in professional bug reports and production incident follow-ups.

lessons.body:
Phase Synthesis & Independent Challenge — Prisma 7.9.1 Architecture, Configuration & Migrations

Mission
Rebuild the capability of Phase 09 without following the exact code line-by-line. The goal is transfer: can you use the ideas when the variable names, UI, or route shape changes?

Required outcome
Integrate Prisma 7.9.1 as a repeatable persistence layer with schema, generated client, adapter/configuration, migrations, and NestJS lifecycle.

Required artifact
Prisma schema + migration history + generated client + NestJS PrismaService connected to TaskFlow PostgreSQL.

Constraints
• Start from the previous phase checkpoint or a fresh branch.
• Use the course architecture boundaries, but do not copy the reference implementation until after your first attempt.
• Keep changes scoped to the capability.
• Preserve validation, authorization, error handling, and observability expectations already earned in earlier phases.
• Record any design decision where more than one implementation is reasonable.

Acceptance criteria
• Can explain schema vs migration vs generated client.
• Can create and inspect a migration.
• Can wire Prisma to NestJS cleanly.
• Can diagnose common connection/migration failures.

Independent build sequence
1. Pin Prisma packages to the course version contract and verify all Prisma package versions match.
2. Initialize Prisma with the intended generated-client output and PostgreSQL configuration.
3. Model one entity, create the first migration, and inspect the SQL before applying it.
4. Generate the client and wire a PrismaService into NestJS with controlled lifecycle.
5. Perform a smoke query through the service, then inspect the created database object independently.
6. Cause a safe migration/configuration failure and practice reading Prisma error codes instead of reinstalling randomly.

Self-review
Compare your implementation to the reference only after the acceptance criteria pass. Differences are not automatically mistakes. For each difference, ask: does it preserve the same contract, security boundary, correctness, maintainability, and operational behavior? Keep the alternative when you can justify it with evidence.

Stretch challenge
Change one assumption: more users, a second tenant, a slow network, an expired session, a concurrent mutation, a deployment restart, or a failed dependency. Predict whether your design still behaves correctly. If not, document the next architectural improvement rather than adding complexity blindly.

Phase exit
Run the relevant checks, inspect Git diff, and write a three-sentence summary: what the system can do now, which boundary owns the new responsibility, and which failure you now know how to diagnose. Only then mark the phase complete.

lessons.body:
Mastery Capstone Lab

This is the transfer exercise for Phase 09: Prisma 7.9.1 Architecture, Configuration & Migrations. The detailed lessons are now closed-book reference material. Your task is to prove that the phase outcome can be reproduced from requirements, repository evidence, and debugging—not by copying a finished implementation.

Target artifact
Prisma schema + migration history + generated client + NestJS PrismaService connected to TaskFlow PostgreSQL.

Acceptance criteria
- Write the behavior and constraints before implementation.
- Identify the owning layer and every boundary crossed.
- Implement the smallest complete vertical slice.
- Verify the happy path from outside the implementation.
- Demonstrate at least one expected failure path.
- Run the phase-relevant quality checks.
- Review the diff for accidental duplication, leaked responsibilities, missing validation/authorization, and hidden environment assumptions.

Evidence packet
Save the command/request used, expected result, actual result, one failure reproduction, the fix, and a short explanation of why the final responsibility belongs where it does. This packet is more valuable than a screenshot of a green page because it demonstrates repeatable engineering reasoning.

Stretch
Change one requirement after the first implementation. Measure which files must change. If a tiny domain change causes unrelated layers to move, use that evidence to discuss coupling before adding another abstraction.
